newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market steady at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market steady at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was fairly slow Wednesday at $70.00 per cwt, steady with Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
USDA reported 4,400 head had sold as 1500 CDT Wednesday in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, bringing the week-to-date total to 87,100 there.
About 1,000 had sold in Kansas, cattle feeders there said.
Many of this week's sales were on Monday and Tuesday, with feedlots in the Panhandle area current and those in Kansas close to current, cattle feeders said.
Many cattle sold earlier this week were being shipped already, fueling ideas that beef demand was strengthening.
Demand for beef was said to be coming from retailers booking for first of the month featuring coming up in two weeks, sources said.

The stronger demand was reflected in expanded slaughter estimates compared with a week ago. Wednesday's slaughter was estimated at 135,000 head and Tuesday's slaughter was revised upward to 128,000 from 125,000, USDA said.
Week-to-date cattle slaughter through Wednesday was pegged at 379,000 head, up from 345,000 a week ago.
